newsitem.title: USA: Data Translation offers digital video unit.
newsitem.headline: Data Translation offers digital video unit.

text.p: Data Translation Inc on Monday unveiled a new version of its consumer-oriented digital video-storage system designed for use with Internet Web pages, multimedia presentations and computer-based training.
The company said its Broadway 2.0 system offered a new method of storing digital video images based on the Digital Versatile Disk (DVD) standard.
The Data Translation product is one of the first to be built around C-Cube Microsystems Inc's digital video chip technology, which was also announced Monday.
The Broadway system is priced at $995, Data Translation said.

The C-Cube system allows full motion video to be compressed in real time at the MPEG-1 industry standard of 30 frames per second, enabling video content from a variety of sources -- including videocassette recorders or camcorders -- to be stored and used on personal computers.

The MPEG 1 system is designed for use in creating and playing back with VHS videocassette quality or desktop computer quality video. It stops short of MPEG 2 standard video, which is a higher-grade standard for broadcast video quality.
